Lambourn and Wesley, "Motorcycle Tire/Road Friction", SAE 2010-01-0054: on dry surfaces peak μ around 1.2, locked-wheel 0.7–0.9 (TRL report PPR496: https://www.trl.co.uk/uploads/trl/documents/PPR496.pdf)
μ table: dry 0.80–0.90, wet 0.50–0.70, gravel 0.60 (gravel slides on itself), earth 0.68 / 0.55

Carter, Rose and Pentecost, "Validation of Equations for Motorcycle and Rider Lean on a Curve", SAE Int. J. Trans. Safety 3(2), 2015, doi:10.4271/2015-01-1422: the basic lean formulas consistently underestimate measured lean; Eqs. (16)–(17) give the tyre-width correction after Cossalter, Motorcycle Dynamics (2006), with t the tyre width
45° of lean corresponds to 1 g; lean = atan(lateral g)

Sharp, Evangelou and Limebeer, "Advances in the modelling of motorcycle dynamics", Multibody System Dynamics 12, 251–283, 2004, doi:10.1023/B:MUBO.0000049195.60868.A2: Magic Formula longitudinal-force fit for a 160/70 ZR17 tyre (Table I, eqs. 1–6); measured masses, inertias and layout of a Suzuki GSX-R1000 and its rider (Tables A.I–A.III, Figure 1); a rider who steers by torque from the lean-angle error (section 6)

Meijaard, Papadopoulos, Ruina and Schwab, "Linearized dynamics equations for the balance and steer of a bicycle: a benchmark and review", Proceedings of the Royal Society A 463, 1955–1982, 2007, doi:10.1098/rspa.2007.1857: the linearised lean and steer equations of the Whipple model (eq. 5.3, Appendix A, Appendix B for the heading and path), and the benchmark parameters, matrices and eigenvalues the tests reproduce (Tables 1 and 2)

Åström, Klein and Lennartsson, "Bicycle dynamics and control", IEEE Control Systems Magazine 25(4), 26–47, 2005, doi:10.1109/MCS.2005.1499389: the inverted-pendulum lean model (eq. 1) that shows why a rider must steer away from a turn to lean into it, and a neuromuscular delay of 0.1 s for steering torque reported from a motorcycle study
